sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Contextual Trigger**: The **Nehru Report (1928)** rejected separate electorates, favoring joint electorates, which Jinnah perceived as a threat to Muslim political representation.
• **Core Objective**: To secure **statutory safeguards** for Muslims in the central and provincial legislatures to prevent 'Hindu majority' domination.
• **Political Shift**: Marked the end of the 'Congress-League' cooperation era and solidified Jinnah's role as the primary spokesperson for Muslim communal interests.
• **Key Metric**: The demands focused on **Federalism**, **Representation**, and **Cultural Autonomy**.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Federal system with residuary powers vested in provinces.
Retention of separate electorates until Muslims opt for joint.
One-third representation for Muslims in the Central Legislature.

items.definition: Jinnah demanded these be vested in the provinces, contradicting the Nehru Report which favored a strong center.
The demand that no bill or resolution should be passed if three-fourths of the members of any community in that body opposed it.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Separation of Sindh**: Demanded Sindh be separated from the Bombay Presidency to create a Muslim-majority province.
• **Provincial Autonomy**: Ensured that all provinces have equal autonomy to protect regional Muslim interests.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Congress viewed these as 'communal' and 'anti-national', leading to a deadlock.
• **Solutions**: The failure of these negotiations paved the way for the Round Table Conferences.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'F-E-R-S' (Federal, Electorates, Residuary, Sindh).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Federal structure, Electorates (Separate), Residuary powers to provinces, Separation of Sindh.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Fourteen Points' with the 'Lucknow Pact'. Remember: Lucknow Pact (1916) was a Congress-League alliance; Fourteen Points (1929) was a rejection of the Congress-led Nehru Report.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Constitutional Communalism' to describe the transition from political cooperation to institutionalized communal demands.

keyTakeaways: The Fourteen Points were a direct reaction to the Nehru Report's rejection of separate electorates.
It solidified the demand for a federal structure with strong provincial autonomy.
It marked the definitive breakdown of the 'Nationalist-Muslim' consensus within the Indian freedom struggle.
